{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 119,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Meet fallback dereferences undefined destinationCalendar",
      "body": "`evt.destinationCalendar` is now `DestinationCalendar[] | null | undefined`. Here `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when no destination calendar exists, but the condition immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. Any booking with `location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar throws a TypeError instead of falling back to daily video."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
      "line": 1078,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Team destination calendars are not added when organizer destination is null",
      "body": "`evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op for `null`, so in a collective event where the organizer has no selected destination but hosts do, all host `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped. EventManager then falls back to the organizer's first connected calendar and host calendars never get the event. Initialize to an array or handle null explicitly."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 256,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Update/delete fallback can never find destination calendar",
      "body": "In the fallback expression `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, `externalCalendarId` is only falsy when the else branch runs, so the predicate always compares against null/undefined and the find returns undefined. The previous implementation used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result, updating (and similarly deleting, line 317) an existing event without an `externalCalendarId` reference passes `undefined` as the Google calendar ID instead of the stored destination calendar, causing API failures or the wrong calendar (delete falls back to primary)."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 168,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Hangout link patch uses undefined calendarId after primary fallback",
      "body": "`calendar.events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || \"primary\"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` uses `selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination matches the credential and creation succeeded on the primary calendar, `selectedCalendar` is undefined, so the patch to add the hangout link is made with an undefined calendarId and fails."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 122,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Collective calendar events use first host's calendar as organizer for every credential",
      "body": "In `createEvent` (and `updateEvent` line 228), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`, even though `selectedCalendar` is correctly looked up by `credentialId`. For a collective event, when the manager creates an event in a non-first host's Google calendar, the organizer attendee email is still set to the first host's `externalId`. The event can be owned by/attributed to the wrong Google account. It should look up the destination whose `credentialId` matches the current credential."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/types/Calendar.d.ts",
      "line": 221,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Required credentialId contract is not honored by most calendar services",
      "body": "The `Calendar` interface now requires `createEvent(event, credentialId)`, and EventManager will call each destination with its credential. However the calendar services changed in this PR (Office365, Lark, BaseCalendarService/CalDAV, and likely other app-store calendars) still choose `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` and ignore `credentialId`. They will always create/update in the first destination in the array, so multi-host collective bookings still send non-first hosts' calendar events to the wrong calendar. Making the new argument mandatory without updating all implementations masks the broken behavior."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
      "line": 454,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Recurring cancellation deletes only first calendar reference for every host",
      "body": "In the recurring branch, for each `reference` in `bookingCalendarReference`, the code loops over all calendar credentials but inside each updated booking it always uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes(\"_calendar\"))`. With multiple calendar references (one per collective host), this always resolves to the first reference. Therefore the second and subsequent host events are never deleted; instead the first host's event is deleted repeatedly with different credentials. It should use the current `reference`/credentialId to select the matching booking reference."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts",
      "line": 249,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Destination calendar webhook payload type changes from null/object to array",
      "body": "The test now expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED where it previously was `null`. Because this field is part of the public webhook payload, existing webhook consumers that expect an object or null will break. This should be called out/migrated as a breaking webhook payload change."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts",
      "line": 249,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests cover multi-destination collective booking/cancel/reschedule",
      "body": "The PR only updates one webhook expectation; the central multi-destination logic in handleNewBooking, EventManager, and handleCancelBooking (including recurring cancellation) has no tests. Given the bug-prone branches, add e2e/unit tests for multiple hosts with different calendar providers and for cancellation/rescheduling."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Meet fallback dereferences undefined destinationCalendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is now `DestinationCalendar[] | null | undefined`. Here `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when no destination calendar exists, but the condition immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. Any booking with `location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar throws a TypeError instead of falling back to daily video.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are not added when organizer destination is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op for `null`, so in a collective event where the organizer has no selected destination but hosts do, all host `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped. EventManager then falls back to the organizer's first connected calendar and host calendars never get the event. Initialize to an array or handle null explicitly.

findings.title: Update/delete fallback can never find destination calendar
findings.body: In the fallback expression `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, `externalCalendarId` is only falsy when the else branch runs, so the predicate always compares against null/undefined and the find returns undefined. The previous implementation used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result, updating (and similarly deleting, line 317) an existing event without an `externalCalendarId` reference passes `undefined` as the Google calendar ID instead of the stored destination calendar, causing API failures or the wrong calendar (delete falls back to primary).

findings.title: Hangout link patch uses undefined calendarId after primary fallback
findings.body: `calendar.events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` uses `selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination matches the credential and creation succeeded on the primary calendar, `selectedCalendar` is undefined, so the patch to add the hangout link is made with an undefined calendarId and fails.

findings.title: Collective calendar events use first host's calendar as organizer for every credential
findings.body: In `createEvent` (and `updateEvent` line 228), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`, even though `selectedCalendar` is correctly looked up by `credentialId`. For a collective event, when the manager creates an event in a non-first host's Google calendar, the organizer attendee email is still set to the first host's `externalId`. The event can be owned by/attributed to the wrong Google account. It should look up the destination whose `credentialId` matches the current credential.

findings.title: Required credentialId contract is not honored by most calendar services
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface now requires `createEvent(event, credentialId)`, and EventManager will call each destination with its credential. However the calendar services changed in this PR (Office365, Lark, BaseCalendarService/CalDAV, and likely other app-store calendars) still choose `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` and ignore `credentialId`. They will always create/update in the first destination in the array, so multi-host collective bookings still send non-first hosts' calendar events to the wrong calendar. Making the new argument mandatory without updating all implementations masks the broken behavior.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes only first calendar reference for every host
findings.body: In the recurring branch, for each `reference` in `bookingCalendarReference`, the code loops over all calendar credentials but inside each updated booking it always uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. With multiple calendar references (one per collective host), this always resolves to the first reference. Therefore the second and subsequent host events are never deleted; instead the first host's event is deleted repeatedly with different credentials. It should use the current `reference`/credentialId to select the matching booking reference.

findings.title: Destination calendar webhook payload type changes from null/object to array
findings.body: The test now expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED where it previously was `null`. Because this field is part of the public webhook payload, existing webhook consumers that expect an object or null will break. This should be called out/migrated as a breaking webhook payload change.

findings.title: No tests cover multi-destination collective booking/cancel/reschedule
findings.body: The PR only updates one webhook expectation; the central multi-destination logic in handleNewBooking, EventManager, and handleCancelBooking (including recurring cancellation) has no tests. Given the bug-prone branches, add e2e/unit tests for multiple hosts with different calendar providers and for cancellation/rescheduling.
